content.TextMessage: Bonjour 47, vous etes dans une base secrete de l'ICA, destinee a l'entrainement au sniper. Votre objectif sera de tuer la ou les cible(s) dans chaque lieu que vous irez, si vous tirer sur un innocent, vous perdez une vie. Si vous perdez toutes vos vies, ou si le chronometre arrive a zero, la mission echouera. Bon entrainement 47.

eventsFunctionsExtensions.name: Billboard
eventsFunctionsExtensions.shortDescription: Rotate 3D objects to appear like 2D sprites.
description: Rotate 3D objects to make them face the camera and appear like 2D sprite.
The 3D racing game example uses this extension ([open the project online](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?project=example://3d-racing-game)).

eventsBasedBehaviors.description: Rotate to always face the camera (only the front face of the cube should be enabled).
eventsBasedBehaviors.name: Billboard

events.comment: Make the instance bottom center seen in the scene editor at the same position in the game after the instance is rotated.

eventsFunctions.description: Rotate the object to the camera. This is also done automatically at the end of the scene events.
eventsFunctions.name: FaceCamera

eventsFunctions.description: Check if the object should rotate on X axis.
eventsFunctions.name: ShouldRotateX

eventsFunctions.description: Change if the object should rotate on X axis.
eventsFunctions.name: SetShouldRotateX

eventsFunctions.description: Check if the object should rotate on Y axis.
eventsFunctions.name: ShouldRotateY

eventsFunctions.description: Change if the object should rotate on Y axis.
eventsFunctions.name: SetShouldRotateY

eventsFunctions.description: Check if the object should rotate on Z axis.
eventsFunctions.name: ShouldRotateZ

eventsFunctions.description: Change if the object should rotate on Z axis.
eventsFunctions.name: SetShouldRotateZ

eventsFunctions.description: Enable texture transparency of the front face.
eventsFunctions.name: EnableTransparency

eventsFunctionsExtensions.name: WithThreeJS
eventsFunctionsExtensions.shortDescription: Create a simple 3D scene.
description: This extension is for creating advanced 3D scenes.
It is not compatible with GDevelop Built-in 3D.
## 📖 How to use
Check out this page.
[WithThreeJs Extension for GDevelop](https://pandako.itch.io/with-threejs-extension-for-gdevelop)

Currently, I'm doing development in between jobs, but if many people support me, I will be able to devote more time to the development.

eventsFunctionsExtensions.shortDescription: This behavior removes the limit on the distance the mouse can move and hides the cursor.
description: This behavior removes the limit on the distance the mouse can move and hides the cursor.
For example, a user can rotate or continue to manipulate an object by moving the mouse endlessly ([open the project online](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?project=example://mouse-pointer-lock)).
Without the pointer lock, the rotation or operation will stop the moment the pointer reaches the edge of the browser or screen.
Game players don't have to worry about leaving the gameplay area or accidentally clicking on another application that moves the mouse focus away from the game.
Locking the pointer locks `CursorX()` and `CursorY()` expressions.
Use `MovementX()` and `MovementY()` instead.

eventsFunctionsExtensions.name: FireBullet
eventsFunctionsExtensions.shortDescription: Fire bullets, manage ammo, reloading and overheating.
description: This extension allows objects to fire bullets. To use it, add the behavior to the object that will shoot, then use the provided action to launch another object as the bullet.
The properties of the behavior can be used to customize:
- Cooldown between shots
- Firing multiple bullets at a time ([open the project online](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?project=example://fire-bullet))
- Ammo management
- Overheat
The speed can be specified when using the actions to fire the bullets.
The bullets are automatically given a permanent force to make them move in the 2D plane (no need to use a linear movement or move them with another behavior).
It can be used for:
- Twin-stick shooters ([open the project online](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?project=example://conviction-of-gun-dude-desktop))
- Shoot'em up ([open the project online](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?project=example://space-shooter))
A simple example shows how to make firing patterns ([open the project online](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?project=example://firing-patterns)).

description: Shake layer cameras with translation, rotation and zoom.
- Short shaking can be used to give impact (explosion, hit)
- Shaking can go indefinitely to set an ambiance (engine vibration, earthquake, pulsing)
- Low frequency shaking allows to simulate slow moving objects (ship rocking back and forth)
Release notes:
- Version 3.0.0
- No adaptation of the game events is needed.
- It fixes an issue when used with scrolling, the amplitude will feel bigger in this case.
- The shaking relies on noise which could feel a bit different.
- This extension can no longer do impulses. For this, another extension "Camera impulse" can be used.

events.comment:
At each frame, the camera must catchup the target by a given ratio (speed)
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - 1) - targetX) * (1 - speed)

The frame rate must not impact on the catch-up speed, we don't want a speed in ratio per frame but a speed ratio per second, like this:
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - 1s) - targetX) * (1 - speed)

Ok, but we still need to process each frame, we can use a exponent for this:
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - timeDelta) - targetX) * (1 - speed)^timeDelta
cameraX(t) = targetX + (cameraX(t - timeDelta) - targetX) * exp(timeDelta * ln((1 - speed)))

pow is probably more efficient than precalculated log if the speed is changed continuously but this might be rare enough.

- automatic "gamepad mapper" behaviors for 2D and 3D movement behaviors (platformer characters, top-down movement, 3D character etc...). Add one of these to the object with the movement behavior (i.e: the player most of the time) and the behavior will then be controlled automatically by the gamepad (it works by reading the gamepad state and simulating controls). No need for additional events to make it work once the behaviors are set up.
The Bomberman-like example handles 4 players with gamepads ([open the project online](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?project=example://goose-bomberman)).
